slice: Honda CRF250R / CRF450R / CRF250RX / CRF450RX 2020-2027, pass 5 (2026-10-25): new researched products not in honda-research.json, p4-gapfill.json, p4-bearings-mounts.json or specialty/*.json, plus 2025-2027 rider/tester feedback.

products.product: RS-12 Stainless Full Exhaust w/ Stainless Muffler, CRF250R/RX 25-27
products.what_it_changes: Same maker claim as titanium version: 'up to +8% HP gain @12,000rpm and up to +8% torque @8650rpm'; header resonator to 'maximize power across the spectrum' (yoshimura-rd.com).
products.caveats: One customer review on the maker page says it was heavier than stock with minimal power gain (single owner, contradicts maker claim). Sold out at time of reading.

products.product: Aluminium silencer, Honda CRF450R 2021-2025

fits.notes: Retailer lists CRF 450 R 2021-2025 incl. 50th Anniversary 2023; also CRF 450 RWE 2021-2025 and R-S 2022-2024

products.what_it_changes: Retailer copy: lighter than stock silencer; HGS systems 'enhance throttle response, improve torque' (ghostbikes.com, not the maker).
supporting_parts: Retailer: 'Full HGS system must be used' (most HGS exhausts not compatible with OEM parts)
products.caveats: Fitment 2025 crosses the 2025 CRF450R exhaust change (new head pipe/muffler per MXA) — confirm with HGS. Retailer says silencer requires the full HGS system. No maker page read.

products.product: X10 ECU (fuel & ignition control), CRF250R

fits.notes: Retailer lists CRF250R 2018-2027 (year selector stops at 2025)

products.what_it_changes: Retailer copy of Vortex claims: 10 pre-programmed fuel/spark maps, three trim switches (low/mid/high throttle, +12.5% to -10% fuel), plug-in to stock harness, V-Boost, more power and easier starting (crfsonly.com).
supporting_parts: Vortex software and interface sold separately for reprogramming
products.caveats: Listing year selector (2018-2025) and fitment section (2018-2027) disagree. 2025 CRF250R has a new ECU configuration (Yoshimura release) — confirm map compatibility. CRF250RX not listed. Closed course only.

products.product: X10 ECU (fuel & ignition control), CRF450RX
products.what_it_changes: Retailer copy: 10 maps, 3 fuel trim switches (+12.5%/-10%), V-Boost, reads stock sensors, claims fewer starting issues/flameouts (crfsonly.com).
products.caveats: Separate SKU from the CRF450R unit (ECU-8H2-450R, crr-018). RX-specific maps. Year range spans the 2021 and 2025 platform changes — confirm with Vortex.

products.product: FMF 4.1 Titanium exhaust & Vortex X10 ECU combo, CRF250R/RX 25-26
products.what_it_changes: Retailer: 'Performance gains vary depending on Throttle and RPM points'; top-end gains and better bottom-end from the 'Power' settings; 10 maps, trim switches (crfsonly.com). No dyno numbers.
products.caveats: Dealer bundle SKU, not a maker part number; combo SKU suggests FMF 041615 (MegaBomb header) + 041619 (slip-on) but the page does not itemise them. Title/body year mismatch.

products.product: SX1 PRO ECU kit for Honda CRF250R 2024 (with SX1 Controller)
variants: Map 1 Racing; Map 2 Racing + GPA traction control level 5

fits.notes: Maker installation guide GD-MIP-0058-AA 'Honda CRF 250 R 2024'

products.what_it_changes: Athena/GET: plug-and-play ECU with two R&D maps, higher rev limiter than stock, maps adjustable via WiGET app (SX1 Connect) or Maya software; GPA traction control (athena.eu install guide; GET press release lists 10 GPA levels, launch control and quickshift via separate sensor).
supporting_parts: GET SX1 Controller (included; OEM blue mode button stops working)
OEM Honda kill switch must stay
Maya software (sold separately) to edit fuel maps

where_to_buy.seller: Athena (maker, press release price for SX1 PRO 4T kit)

products.caveats: Kit part number not stated in the guide; the US price is the generic SX1 PRO 4T kit price from the press release. Other CRF250R years not confirmed here. Racing use only.

products.product: Performance linkage, Honda CRF450R 2021- / CRF250R 2022-
products.what_it_changes: No claims on the page (ratio or sag effect not stated).
products.caveats: Only the title gives fitment; end year unknown, and 2025+ CRF450R linkage changes are not addressed. No price shown. Search-result page title says 'Adjustable performance Linkage'.

products.product: Batfly EPTA 270 OS front rotor, CRF250R 19-27
products.what_it_changes: Braking (retailer copy): AL7075-T6 carrier, new connecting elements replacing pins to reduce deformation, radially sliding stems for more even disc temperature and more direct feel; MXGP riders reported improved feel/power.
supporting_parts: Oversize ('OS') rotors normally need a caliper relocation bracket — not stated on this page
products.caveats: Diameter only implied by name (270). Whether a bracket is included is not stated. CRF450R fitment not listed on this page.

products.product: Brake disc kit oversize 280mm front, Honda CRF250R / CRF450R 15-
products.what_it_changes: Retailer copy: larger outer diameter gives more braking power; widely used in AMA SX and MXGP (maciag-offroad.com).
supporting_parts: Kit includes matching caliper adapter, rotor and pads (retailer)
products.caveats: No Galfer part number shown (only EAN 8400170097091 and shop number SID130392). Open-ended '15-' fitment expanded here to 2020-2027 as listed; 2025+ and 2027 fork/caliper changes not confirmed; RX not mentioned. Sold out when read. Galfer maker tables previously redirected (README).

products.product: Triple clamps red, 22mm offset, CRF 2021/2022-25 (S2421)
products.what_it_changes: Scar (distributor copy): CNC 7075-T6 aluminium, four bar positions on the top clamp, improved strength/rigidity and control; used by factory teams (oro2u.com).
supporting_parts: Includes top clamp, bottom clamp, pressed stem, lower bearing
products.caveats: Fitment stops at 2025; 2026 (same chassis as 2025) not listed and 2027 is a new frame. Offset is stock 22mm, so it changes stiffness/bar position rather than trail.

products.product: ROCS Pro triple clamps 22-24mm adjustable offset, Honda CRF450R 21-24 / CRF250R 22-24
products.what_it_changes: Xtrig claims (dealer copy): opposing-clamp design reduces fork-tube deformation, self-locking clamp resists fork twist, split layout keeps controlled flex; adjustable 22-24mm offset, bolted stem (tokyomods.com).
products.caveats: Different product from the fixed-offset ROCS Tech (501330101401). Dealer lists no 2025+ fitment; RX models not named. Stock status unclear.

products.product: Aluminum skid plate, Honda CRF450R (SKU by year range)
products.what_it_changes: Seller copy: 0.160in 5052-H32 aluminum, bolts on with Ricochet hardware, no drilling (traderhank.com).
products.caveats: Price shown is 2023-2026 clear anodize ($150.98; black $183.98; 2021-22 $155.98/$188.98; 2017-20 $148.98/$188.98). SKUs are short Ricochet numbers; maker page not read. Note the year split at 2023 (not 2021/2025 as for most CRF450R parts). RX not listed.

products.product: Pro Circuit Ti-6 & Vortex X10 ECU combo, CRF250R/RX 22-26
products.what_it_changes: Retailer: 10 fuel/spark maps, +12.5%/-10% trims, 'more power, better power, easier starting'; Ti-6 meets AMA amateur noise but not FIM sound limits (crfsonly.com).
products.caveats: Bundle SKU only; components not itemised on page. Note: not FIM sound-legal per page.

products.product: EMS fork spring kit, Honda CRF250R/CRF450R (Showa 49mm)
products.what_it_changes: Retailer copy: range of rates to fine-tune comfort vs performance; no performance data.
products.caveats: Rate options and per-rate part numbers not listed. Title (17-23) and table (17-24) disagree. 2025+ (5.0 N/mm stock, 2027 5.2) not listed.

products.product: RS-12 Titanium Full Exhaust w/ Titanium Muffler, CRF250R/RX 25-27
variants: SA-21-K / SA-20-K spark arrester sold separately
products.what_it_changes: Yoshimura claims 'up to +8% HP gain @12,000rpm and up to +8% torque @8650rpm' vs stock; hydroformed muffler 'lighter and stronger'; press release states max +8.0% hp and +9.0% torque (yoshimura-rd.com; Vital MX press release).
products.caveats: Maker page showed 'Sold Out - Contact Us' with pre-order. Maker lists CRF250RX only 2025-2026 (2027 RX not listed). No weight figure. Closed-course only. Press release: https://www.vitalmx.com/news/press-release/yoshimura-releases-all-new-rs-12-system-2025-honda-crf250r

products.product: Evolution Line titanium full system, CRF250R 18-20 / CRF250RX 18-21

fits.notes: Title only: CRF250RX 18-21 (fitment fields list CRF250 2018-2020)

products.what_it_changes: Retailer copy: all-titanium system to maximize engine performance and reduce weight; no figures.
supporting_parts: Spark arrester, welded bracket, titanium end cap mentioned
products.caveats: Part number read from the store code A|1040-S-H2MET12-CIQTA|0, not a labelled MPN. Predecessor of S-H2MET13-FDHLTA (2022+). Closed course only.

fits.notes: Listed on Teknik's fitment-matched page for 2026 CRF250R; title is fork-specific (Showa 49mm)

products.what_it_changes: Title only: holeshot with one snap-in position; no claims.
products.caveats: Fitment comes from the shop's model filter, not the maker. 55mm refers to the fork outer-tube clamp size presumably; not stated. Teknik lists the part on a fitment-matched page for a later model-year than the title states; price not shown ('Special Order'). Trust the title years.

products.caveats: Fitment from shop filter only. Teknik lists the part on a fitment-matched page for a later model-year than the title states; price not shown ('Special Order'). Trust the title years.

products.what_it_changes: Title only (adjustable offset).

products.what_it_changes: Title only.

products.what_it_changes: Title only (Showa genuine parts / GPE billet lugs).

products.what_it_changes: Hinson claims (retailer copy): billet 6061-T6 hard-coated parts with 'five times the wear resistance to stock', better heat dissipation, spins truer, helps eliminate chatter.
products.caveats: PN from store SKU (H|1629-HC794-1801|0), MSliders listing and a Firestorm image filename; maker-site confirmation not obtained. Firestorm lists the same kit for CRF250RX 2019-2021 (title only). Different kit from 2022+ (HC894-2201).

products.product: EMS Moto front fork kit 0.50 kg/mm, 45.00mm OD x 472mm (pair)
variants: 0.50 kg/mm (other rates in range not listed on page)

products.what_it_changes: Eibach: ultra-lightweight to reduce unsprung mass, each spring tested, high linearity and consistency; made in USA (eibach.com).
products.caveats: Maker fitment is Works Edition only; Eibach 'does not guarantee fitment' on unlisted applications. 0.50 kg/mm is ~4.9 N/mm, softer than the 5.0 N/mm stock CRF450R spring testers already find soft - check rate before buying. Same 45 x 472mm size as Teknik listing 903 (cr5-024).

products.product: EMS fork spring kit, Honda CRF450R 17-23 (discontinued)
products.what_it_changes: No claims beyond 'tailored rates'; rate not listed.
products.caveats: Marked 'DISCONTINUED - No Longer Available'. Kept for owners identifying installed springs. Rate unknown; by Eibach numbering likely a ~0.56 kg/mm (5.5 N/mm) rate - NOT confirmed.

feedback.author: customer (name not recorded)
feedback.conditions: Owner review on maker page; bike year not stated (part fits 2025-2027)
feedback.observed: Reviewer says the system was heavier than stock and gave minimal power gain.

feedback.author: MXA Staff
feedback.conditions: Stock suspension settings; before the clamps testers had lowered forks to flush and dropped race sag to 107mm because the stock bike felt too sensitive
feedback.observed: With the 23.5mm clamps the chassis felt more settled, suspension worked better over acceleration and braking bumps, more consistent and predictable at speed; MXA: 'consistency, confidence and comfort', but 'the Honda needs more than triple clamps'. No complaints.
feedback.measured: Offset 23.5mm vs stock 22mm; bar mount positions 12.5mm / 6mm ahead of stem, optional 15.5mm mount; prices: clamps $649.90, bar mounts $104.95, stem nut $34.95 (sold separately); race sag 107mm

feedback.author: Trevor Hunter (story Jimmy Lewis)
feedback.conditions: First impression at Spring Creek MX, Minnesota: loamy, soft, tight rutted corners; 200 lb test rider; final suspension verdict pending dry California dirt
feedback.observed: Smooth, linear 'sneaky fast' engine; reduced engine braking (clutch-damper slipper function + new mapping) helps corner entry; taller, wider-spread 5-speed (2nd often usable in ruts); steering less twitchy, slightly heavier turn-in; plush Showa; bulky grips and slippery seat cover; map button must be held several seconds near idle.
feedback.measured: Ride height ~102mm stock; forks lowered 2.5mm in clamps; fork/shock compression +/-1 click by rider aggression; fork rebound +1 click; shock HSC softened 1/4 turn to level the bike

feedback.author: Chris Pomeroy
feedback.conditions: Media first ride, Spring Creek MX (long sand whoops); Honda test rider Trey Canard present
feedback.observed: Calmer, more stable and predictable than 2025/26 ('busy' per Canard); longer-pulling power, 2nd/3rd feel longer; much less engine braking; front holds up better in braking-to-acceleration transitions.
feedback.measured: Fork springs 5.0 -> 5.2 N/mm; bore +1mm; tank 1.9 gal (was 1.7); frame rigidity ~+10%; footpegs 5mm rearward; ~70% new frame parts; new swingarm, chain slider, shock linkage, rear hub, airbox and filter; DBS (Dynamic Blow System) fork valve; new rear tire size

feedback.author: Travis Fant (with Mark Tilley)
feedback.conditions: Glen Helen video test; 2026 unchanged from 2025
feedback.observed: Strong low-end torque, peak power behind Yamaha/KTM; still a little soft; testers stiffened the front and slid forks down in the clamps. Suggested mods by brand: Pro Circuit or Ride Engineering linkage, FMF/Dubach/Yoshimura/Akrapovic exhaust; FCP offset bearings helped stability; 2025 parts transfer to 2026.
feedback.measured: Rear sag 107mm; fork height change not quantified; MSRP $9,699

feedback.author: Caleb Tennant
feedback.conditions: US launch (Fox Raceway / Pala): muddy rutted pro track and smoother vet track
feedback.observed: Plush on vet track, stiffened slightly for pro track; front can be twitchy in long choppy corners; wanted more torque in deep conditions; aggressive map sharpens response and revs but little extra bottom; standard or TC map for slick/muddy.
feedback.measured: No numeric settings published

feedback.author: Caleb Tennant
feedback.conditions: Same US launch (muddy pro track, smoother vet track)
feedback.observed: Balanced, tracked well in ruts, no changes needed; smoother throttle connection than past years; aggressive map livelier, standard map for hard-pack/slippery; launch control effective.
feedback.measured: Sag 'set correctly from the start' but no value given

feedback.author: Gardner Tarlow
feedback.conditions: Weekend-warrior review: Glen Helen practice, other tracks and dry tight/fast single track; settings rechecked after ~6+ hours
feedback.observed: Strong cornering and stability; forearm fatigue that improved with setting changes; cable clutch feels dated (Honda hydraulic clutch conversion mentioned); full 2.1 gal tank and wide shrouds raise CG slightly; used Dunlop MX34 front later.
feedback.measured: Stock rec: fork C10 R14, height 5mm; shock HS 2 1/3, LS 10, R15; sag 105mm. As received: fork height 6mm, sag 102mm (104mm after 6 h). Final: fork C11 R13; shock HS 2 2/3. Clamp pinch bolts 16/15 -> 12/10 lb (16/13.5 Nm). Maps: 3 for motos, 1 fast single track, 2 tight technical.

feedback.author: Andrew Oldar
feedback.conditions: Dirt Rider in-house dyno after riding at MotoVentures; no correction/fuel details given
feedback.observed: Smooth, easy power; 2025 development mainly chassis/suspension.
feedback.measured: 37.7 hp, 18.0 lb-ft at the rear wheel (+0.6 hp, +0.2 lb-ft vs 2023); rpm not stated

feedback.author: Ron Lawson
feedback.conditions: MotoVentures (Anza, CA) tight trials-style terrain, mostly under 24 mph
feedback.observed: Out of its element in tight trails: hard to control at low speed, power hits hard around 12 mph, even the softest of 3 maps aggressive; very planted at speed; suspension only slightly softer than MX.
feedback.measured: Rear sprocket 50T (vs 49T on CRF450R)

feedback.author: Ron Lawson
feedback.conditions: MotoVentures tight trails
feedback.observed: Better suited to tight trails; off-road map smooths the transition into the power; gentle, controllable low end with enough to climb obstacles.
feedback.measured: No settings published

feedback.author: Trevor Hunter
feedback.conditions: Product test; date from page metadata (last modified)
feedback.observed: Softer, less harsh front, better bump compliance; more stable at speed and on brakes; less oversteer/knifing; less playful than stock; pricey and complicates under-bar stabilizers.
feedback.measured: Offset 23.5 vs 22mm; bars 5mm lower, 3mm forward (claimed); with stock clamps forks flush; with RE clamps forks at +2mm; flush to +2mm by terrain; clamps felt like a few clicks softer compression so testers added a few clicks; price $674.90

feedback.author: Mat Boyd
feedback.conditions: 2 hours; 95 kg, 38-year-old rider moving down from a 450; stock setup
feedback.observed: Very quick steering; stock grips uncomfortable; plush suspension still holds up at 95 kg (judged better than the CRF450R's); soft off the bottom but revs well - wants more low-down torque. Planned mods: lock-on grips, GET ECU, airbox changes.
feedback.measured: No settings published

feedback.product: GET ECU (2024 CRF250R unit remapped for 2025), Wi-Fi module
feedback.author: Mat Boyd
feedback.conditions: 5 hours; dyno mapping with O2 sensor
feedback.observed: No 2025 GET kit existed, so a 2024 unit was remapped; the 2024 map did not suit the 2025's new airbox/filter. Removing the airbox backfire screen and enlarging the cover opening improved response; final dyno map needed no on-track changes. Second injector from the GET 2024 kit planned.
feedback.measured: Map targeting ~14:1 AFR; leaner low, richer high; more timing low, retarded as revs rise; separate hard-pack, mud and sand maps via GET Wi-Fi. No power figures yet.
feedback.other_mods: ODI grips; airbox backfire screen removed, larger hole in airbox cover

feedback.author: Will Embree
feedback.conditions: Fox Raceway National track, prepped then beat up; 160 lb rider; Pirelli Scorpion MX32 Mid-Soft
feedback.observed: Stiffer frame/clamps/fork tubes: stable, precise, comfortable; at 105mm sag front more upright and slightly more stable over rollers but he prefers 102mm for MX; Map 2 chosen (Map 3 'a bit too snappy'); new airbox has a wide left vent so drilling the cover is unnecessary but filter needs more frequent cleaning.
feedback.measured: Sag 102mm (Showa recommendation) and 105mm; claimed wet weight 234 lb; MSRP $8,299

feedback.author: Ryan Nitzen
feedback.conditions: Fox Raceway launch, prime conditions; traction control not tested
feedback.observed: Gained low-end torque from new airbox, exhaust and ratios; 2nd/3rd noticeably longer; Aggressive map preferred; plusher fork, planted shock; more precise in braking bumps.
feedback.measured: Final drive 13/50 (spec sheet); no clicker or sag values

feedback.author: Kris Keefer
feedback.conditions: 2023 450 MX baseline settings for roughly 160-200 lb riders
feedback.observed: Fork may be soft over 180 lb; heavier fork spring improves traction and stability; stock 56 N/mm shock spring adequate.
feedback.measured: Fork: 5.1 N/mm (one 5.2 on one side), height flush-2mm, comp 12 out, reb 11 out. Shock: 56 N/mm stock, sag 105mm, LSC 10 out, HSC 2 out, reb 11 out.

feedback.author: Mattia Carpi
feedback.conditions: Arco di Trento (MX Trentino), sunny ~35C, drying track; 95 kg, 180 cm tester
feedback.observed: Much softer, progressive low/mid power with strong top; 2nd gear more usable; new clutch reduces engine braking on entry; Normal map recommended, Hard 'not for everyone'; more open steering head, ~1cm longer wheelbase, more stable, slight front bias remains; strong progressive Nissin front brake; fork soft and low in stroke - closed compression slightly and opened rebound; shock softened slightly (more HSC spring preload internally makes adjustments more effective). Works Edition (December) to get Yoshimura exhaust, machined head, own map, Kashima suspension.
feedback.measured: No numeric settings or power figures

feedback.author: Gray Van Dyke
feedback.conditions: Launch news (not a ride test)
feedback.observed: All-new Unicam engine (larger bore/shorter stroke, new piston, cam, ports), rubber-damper Back Torque Limiter clutch, all-new frame (~30% carryover), new shock and revised linkage ratio, updated Nissin brakes, HRC launch + HSTC. Works Edition (Oct): hand-ported head, Yoshimura exhaust, special ECU settings, Hinson clutch basket. No compatibility statement.
feedback.measured: Claims: peak hp +10.3%, torque +3.7%; engine 17mm slimmer and ~6 lb lighter; 238 lb wet (~10 lb lighter); price $10,099 (page link says $11,000 - unresolved); Works Edition $12,999

feedback.author: Ryan Nitzen
feedback.conditions: Spring Creek MX first ride; back-to-back with 2026 (conclusions only in video)
feedback.observed: Reshaped seat, larger tank, new plastics, meets updated AMA sound rules - affects seat, graphics, plastics and exhaust compatibility (inference, not stated).
feedback.measured: Nearly 10 lb lighter than 2026, ~6 lb from engine (Honda figure); tank 1.9 gal

feedback.author: MotoPinas.com staff
feedback.conditions: Model-launch news, not a test
feedback.observed: Lists for the 2025 CRF250RX: 70% new frame, new Showa suspension, two-piston Nissin front caliper, revised intake/exhaust and PGM-FI, 3-level HSTC, launch control, engine mode button, 3 maps and an 'HRC Setting tool'. Tank unchanged at 8 L.
feedback.measured: No settings or rates

parts.product: GET SX1-type ECU from the 2024 CRF250R kit, remapped on the dyno, Wi-Fi map switching
parts.purpose: Low-end torque; maps for hard-pack, mud and sand
parts.observed: 2024 map did not suit the 2025 airbox; remapped to ~14:1 AFR, no on-track changes needed

parts.product: Airbox backfire screen removed, larger hole cut in airbox cover

common_first_mods: Offset clamps 23.5mm (Ride Engineering) on 2021-2023 CRF450R/RX: more settled and predictable at speed, softer front feel; testers then run forks +2mm and add a few clicks of compression (MXA 2023, Dirt Bike Test 2023).

Fork lowered in the clamps / stiffened front on 2025-2027 CRF450R (Dirt Bike Magazine 2026: forks slid down, 107mm sag; Dirt Bike Test 2027: forks down 2.5mm, +1 rebound, HSC -1/4 turn; Moto.it 2027: more compression, less rebound).
Reduced triple-clamp pinch-bolt torque on the 2025 CRF250RX (16/15 -> 12/10 lb) and chassis torque reductions (Keefer Inc, Gardner Tarlow).
ECU replacement or reflash for more bottom-end on the 2025+ CRF250R (ADB long-term: GET; Vortex X10 ECU-8H2-250R and dealer reflash services listed).
Linkage (Pro Circuit or Ride Engineering) and FCP offset bearings suggested for the 2025-2026 CRF450R (Dirt Bike Magazine 2026).
gaps: Target of 60-100 new products not reached: 30 new products. The shared web-search budget for this turn ran out after about 40 searches, and pages linked from fetched pages (MXA race tests 2026 CRF250/CRF450 and 2027 CRF450 tested, Keefer 2027 CRF450R/CRF250R articles, Teknik category pages, MXA tag pages) were refused for lack of fetch approval.

No new maker-confirmed part numbers for 2025+ CRF450R from Pro Circuit (procircuit.com not reachable) or FMF (fmfracing.com not tried; FMF 2025+ numbers already in specialty/engine.json from dealers).
Pro Circuit Ti-6 BC Pro 0312545BC: Cycle Gear's fitment block lists CRF450R/RX 2021-2026 together with dozens of other bikes (aggregated across variants), so per-model fitment remains unreliable.
